state_summary.one_line: Aarav begins June with fresh salary cash in HDFC, a modest ICICI buffer, meaningful Axis card pressure, small Simpl usage, and enough liquid fund value to survive two stress redemptions without looking wealthy.
state_summary.starting_liquidity_posture: Visible deposits total ₹172450 across HDFC and ICICI. Early-June cash obligations total ₹166440, so June is payable from visible deposits but leaves only about ₹6010 deposit buffer before ordinary daily spending.
state_summary.starting_credit_posture: Axis current outstanding is high at ₹137850, latest statement balance is ₹96500, and ₹96500 is due by 2025-06-09 with no severe default. The latest statement balance includes a ₹18500 revolved balance from an earlier partial-payment month, plus current-cycle statemented purchases and charges.
state_summary.starting_investment_posture: UTI SIP folio has accumulated prior investments worth about ₹184200, while ICICI liquid fund remains untouched at the start with ₹73500, sufficient for two later redemptions of around ₹30000 each.
state_summary.why_this_starting_state_is_realistic: May salary has recently arrived into HDFC, but June rent, SIP, card due, staff payments, maintenance, mother medicines, electricity, and recurring card autopays are still ahead. Aarav can pay early-June cash obligations without fake rescue inflows, but doing so leaves a very thin deposit buffer of about ₹6010 before daily spending. The liquid fund provides emergency fallback without making him look wealthy or comfortable.
